exact_statement: For positive a(epsilon),L(epsilon) with finite limits log a(epsilon)/log epsilon -> alpha and log L(epsilon)/log epsilon -> 0 as epsilon downarrow 0, b(epsilon)=a(epsilon)L(epsilon) has log exponent alpha.
proof_or_counterexample: log b/log epsilon = log a/log epsilon + log L/log epsilon; taking the limits gives alpha. This was independently rederived by w521.
remaining_gap: No exact value of alpha or d_gamma follows; the lemma only preserves a known exponent.

exact_statement: For any metric D and 0<a<1, D^a is a metric with the same topology and dim_H(X,D^a)=dim_H(X,D)/a. It preserves constant-shift and coordinate-change identities after changing xi to a*xi, but is generally not a length metric.
assumptions: D is a metric on X
Hausdorff dimension uses the standard diameter-power convention
source: w520/ATTEMPT.md, snowflake lemma candidate and stated boundary
proof_or_counterexample: Concavity gives (u+v)^a<=u^a+v^a. A D^a-cover at mesh delta corresponds to a D-cover at mesh delta^(1/a), with s-power costs equal to as-power costs. On [0,1], n equal intervals have D^a-path length n^(1-a)->infinity, so the snowflake need not satisfy LQG's length-space axiom.
remaining_gap: Only reduced scalar identities are covered; this is not a second LQG metric and does not determine d_gamma.

exact_statement: If (X,D) is compact and mu is a probability measure with c_epsilon r^(d+epsilon) <= mu(B_D(x,r)) <= C_epsilon r^(d-epsilon) simultaneously for every x in X and all sufficiently small r for each epsilon in (0,d), then dim_H(X,D)=d.
source: owner-own-work; elementary covering and mass-distribution derivation in w521/ATTEMPT.md
proof_or_counterexample: Upper bound: maximal r-separated set has at most c_epsilon^(-1)(r/2)^(-d-epsilon) points by disjoint-ball mass, and its r-balls cover X. Lower bound: any small-diameter cover has total (d-epsilon)-cost at least 1/C_epsilon by the upper ball-mass bound.
remaining_gap: No explicit f(gamma) all-center metric-ball estimate is proved for LQG; no parent-problem conclusion.
